**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/24 (Wed) 16:18  
[USER] User asked how to access a drive in macOS.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To access a drive in macOS, connect the drive to your Mac, and it should appear on your desktop or in Finder under "Computer" or "/Volumes."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If connecting a network drive, a username and password may be required. If the drive is formatted for a different OS, third-party software may be needed.  
[USER] User asked how to show the desktop quickly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To show the desktop quickly, place the pointer in the right corner of the Dock and swipe right with three fingers, or press the "F11" key.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] These gestures and shortcuts can be customized in "Trackpad" or "Keyboard" preferences in "System Preferences."  
[USER] User mentioned inserting an SD card into a USB-C dongle and connecting it to macOS but did not know how to use it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To access the SD card, connect the dongle, and it should appear on the desktop or in Finder under "Devices." Double-click to open and manage files.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ensure the SD card is properly inserted and the dongle is connected; if locked, unlock it to access contents.  
[USER] User asked how to press F11 with a native keyboard in macOS.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The "F11" key is not present on native Apple keyboards; instead, use "Control + F3" to show the desktop.  
[USER] User asked for the key to open Terminal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To open Terminal, press "Command + Space" to open Spotlight, type "Terminal," and press "Enter."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Alternatively, access Terminal from Applications > Utilities or Launchpad.  
[USER] User requested instructions on how to create a keyboard shortcut to open Terminal using Automator.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To create a shortcut in Automator, open Automator, choose "Service," and use "Run AppleScript" with the code to activate Terminal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Save the service, then assign a keyboard shortcut in "System Preferences" > "Keyboard" > "Shortcuts" > "Services."  
[USER] User asked how to delete a file in Finder by selecting it and pressing delete.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To delete a file in Finder, select the file and press the "Delete" key or right-click and choose "Move to Trash."
